feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital leadership roles: the experience is relevant, progressive, and supported by concrete platforms, scope, and outcomes. It reads clearly overall, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, and a few style/grammar inconsistencies reduce polish.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior positioning: the headline, summary, and career progression strongly support a digital platform/communications leadership profile.  
- Good credibility signals: named employer, long tenure, measurable scale (10,000+ pages, 3.5M page views, 50+ publishers), and specific tools/platforms.  
- Broad but coherent skill set: strategy, governance, analytics, CMS, multimedia, and AI/search are presented as an integrated leadership capability.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition and tighten structure: “digital strategy/operations/governance/workflows” appears often across sections; consolidate Topline Skills vs. Technical + IT to avoid duplication.  
- Add more outcome-focused impact: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than results; include clearer business/user outcomes where possible.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “organization-wide” and “front-end” are consistent, but capitalization is mixed (“Coleman DAVIS” vs normal title case); “Ranked among the top public universities…” is weak filler; punctuation/bullet formatting in work entries is uneven. No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible positioning with clear seniority and sector focus, but it reads slightly broad and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and work experience. Tightening it around distinctive value and scale will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “Senior digital leader” with a more specific identity tied to enterprise platforms and public-sector communications.
- Add one concrete scale marker from recent experience to increase credibility.
- Trim the long list of functions; group related areas to improve flow and avoid sounding like a skills inventory.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital platform and communications systems leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web ecosystems for high-volume, mission-driven public-sector organizations. Leads website transformation, digital governance, analytics infrastructure, editorial operations, and AI-enabled content discovery—most recently overseeing a 10,000+ page Drupal migration supporting 3.5M annual page views and 50+ internal publishers.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle; use the intro to add specificity instead.
- The current function list repeats core competencies almost verbatim.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if phrased as broader capability areas and trimmed to avoid repeating near-identical wording elsewhere.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and simplify wording: “Enterprise web modernization” instead of “Enterprise website modernization.”
- Replace generic items with clearer, higher-value categories: “Digital governance, editorial workflows, and publishing systems” and “Analytics, dashboards, and reporting infrastructure.”
- Tighten channel language: “Multi-channel communications and campaign operations” is cleaner than “communications operations.”
- Suggested rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance, editorial workflows & publishing systems • Analytics, dashboards & reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications & campaign operations • AI-enabled search & content discovery • Workflow automation & platform integrations • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production & livestream operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Strong overlap with the header summary and all four Topline Skills blocks; consider shortening this section or using it to emphasize only the most distinctive strengths.
- “AI-enabled search and content experiences” is already reinforced in Recent Projects; “content discovery” avoids repetition.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it currently repeats themes already covered in Work Experience and reads a bit dense for a footer. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and format each item as a concise achievement-focused bullet.
- Make descriptions more specific with outcomes, scale, or audience where possible (for example, users served, campaign purpose, or organizational impact).
- Standardize style and parallel structure: start each project with a strong verb and avoid long feature lists.
- Spell out “10 × 20-foot” consistently and consider “AI-powered” instead of “AI-enabled” for smoother phrasing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, anniversary campaign, and advocacy video series all overlap with Work Experience; keep this section shorter and more project/outcome-focused rather than restating responsibilities.
- “Advocacy Video Series” closely echoes earlier NACo video work; clarify whether this is a recent consulting project or remove to avoid repetition.

items.title: Core Competencies

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical breadth, but it reads as a responsibilities list. Tighten it around 3–5 outcome-oriented bullets and emphasize what is new or higher-level versus your NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + client type + mandate in one line: “Embedded as a full-time freelance consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital strategy, Drupal platform improvements, and communications operations.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground impact: “Redesigned digital workflows, analytics, and governance to improve coordination across organization-wide communications.”
- Combine overlapping web/CMS points: “Built Drupal campaign experiences, including microsites, modular content components, and member toolkits; provided front-end implementation and troubleshooting for high-traffic public web properties.”
- Keep the AI work as a differentiator and add metrics if possible: “Led AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval strategy, structured content model, and discovery UX to improve findability.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” overlaps heavily with NACo Director role; keep only if you can show a distinct result or newer capability.
- “CMS development/front-end implementation” may duplicate skills sections unless tied to a business outcome.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It would be sharper if the opening were more concise and the bullets emphasized outcomes, team/operational leadership, and what changed under your direction.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening with: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Tighten and front-load impact: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-oriented: add growth, engagement, open/click rates, production volume, or campaign results if available; otherwise shorten to avoid generic phrasing.
- Strengthen operational bullets with results: e.g., “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio, reducing external production reliance and expanding advocacy/event content capacity,” and “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting to improve leadership visibility and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Video as a recurring channel” overlaps with the prior NACo role; keep this entry focused on studio buildout and scale.
- Governance/workflow language overlaps with consulting and earlier NACo entries; emphasize enterprise scope here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later NACo director role and earlier digital media role. Make it more about what you specifically built or scaled at this level, with sharper outcomes and less generic “helped improve” phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + level: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial operations and advocacy messaging for a national association audience.”
- Replace weak verbs: change “helped scale,” “strengthened,” and “helped improve” to direct ownership verbs like “managed,” “built,” “standardized,” “launched,” or “streamlined.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: newsletter audience growth/open rates, video cadence/views, publishing turnaround time, number of teams/stakeholders coordinated.
- Possible rewrite:
- Managed day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social media and video for NACo’s national advocacy and member communications.
- Oversaw four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Standardized editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital communications across web, email, social media and video” is already stated in the 2022–2024 role; keep this version focused on execution and workflow-building.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the channel, not originating it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is broad and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level leadership areas most supported by the recent consultant and director roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, outcome-oriented phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & platform modernization
- Editorial governance & cross-functional content operations
- Multi-channel communications leadership across web, email, social & video
- Public-sector, membership & advocacy messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy, usability & discovery
- Use “content operations” instead of “content planning” to sound more senior and align with recent governance/workflow work.
- Add “platform modernization” and “usability & discovery” to reflect the Drupal migration and AI-enabled search work.
- If space is tight, cut “public-sector” or “audience-centered” rather than repeating generic “digital strategy.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Multi-channel communications leadership” duplicate the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Editorial systems and governance” overlaps with “Editorial workflow design”; consider using only one version across sections.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads as a raw tool list rather than a senior, impact-oriented skills statement. It also overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section, so this version should stay higher-level and emphasize current strengths.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms (WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages)”
- Prioritize recent, differentiating strengths: “CMS modernization, front-end implementation, API integrations, workflow automation, and AI-enabled search”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; avoid repeating exact tool lists in both places.
- jQuery may date the profile unless it is still directly relevant to current work.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster that aligns well with the most recent NACo leadership role, but it reads as a generic tool list. Tighten it to emphasize decision-making, measurement, and optimization outcomes rather than just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to capability-first, e.g. “Analytics strategy, KPI design & executive reporting.”
- Group tools more cleanly: “GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, BigQuery.”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with stronger business language like “Executive dashboards” or “Performance reporting for leadership.”
- Consider revised line: “Analytics strategy & KPI design • Executive dashboards & performance reporting • GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, BigQuery • SEO and conversion/performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Data analytics & reporting” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating that exact phrasing.
- The NACo Director role already names these tools, so this skills item should summarize capabilities, not restate the same list too mechanically.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it reads generic and overlaps with both the Core Competencies section and multiple NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and use sharper phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: “Broadcast video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio system operation • Virtual event production workflows”
- Consider upgrading “Video production and editing” to “Broadcast video production” or “End-to-end video production” to sound more senior and aligned with the in-house studio achievement.
- Combine “Hybrid and virtual event production” with livestreaming to reduce repetition and improve scanability.
- If space allows elsewhere, add scale/context instead of more tools, e.g., “studio buildout” or “recurring advocacy programming,” since impact is already proven in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia & live event production” already appears in Core Competencies; keep this version more specific/technical.
- “Studio operations” and “PTZ camera systems” may feel too tactical if you want a more leadership-level CV tone.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Since recent roles show strongest Drupal-led impact, this item should emphasize platform depth or be tightened to avoid repetition.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to signal proficiency level and recency, e.g.: “Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites, governance) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, prioritize by strength/usage: put Drupal first and consider dropping GitHub Pages if it was minor compared with enterprise CMS work.
- Consider adding a brief qualifier instead of a pure list: “Enterprise CMS: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages; static publishing: GitHub Pages”
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; “Power Pages” is fine, but avoid mixing platform names with broader capabilities here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same core platforms.
- Drupal appears repeatedly across recent experience; avoid restating it without adding context or specialization.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools most relevant to recent work and group items more strategically.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery
- Add a second line/group: Technical tooling: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- If accurate, add light outcome/context language elsewhere in the CV rather than here, e.g., “used for CMS enhancements, campaign microsites, automation, and deployment workflows”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless older formatting is used consistently; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates Topline Skills [2] (“HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery,” “API integrations”); keep one more strategic and one more tool-specific
- “Workflow automation” in Topline Skills may already cover part of GitHub Actions/Cloudflare Workers if described elsewhere

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow design capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize function, e.g. “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Systems.”
- Tighten to the most relevant tools and group by use case: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira/Asana • Slack/Teams.”
- If space allows, add light context instead of a pure list: “Built and managed workflow automation, project tracking, and cross-team collaboration systems using Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Slack, and Teams.”
- Drop older/lower-signal tools unless they are current and important; Basecamp and Trello feel less aligned with the senior, recent experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Jira, Asana, Basecamp, and Trello are partially redundant as project-management tools; listing all four weakens impact.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this item is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses a chance to signal scale or functional strength. Since recent roles emphasize email operations, frame these as platforms you’ve actively used to run member communications and engagement programs.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms
- Replace with: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, strengthen with function: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (campaign automation, segmentation, journeys) • Higher Logic (member email/community engagement) • Mailchimp
- Keep it concise; only add descriptors that reflect hands-on use in recent roles, not generic platform familiarity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Email leadership already appears in multiple NACo roles, so avoid adding broad claims like “newsletter management” here unless tied to platform-specific capability.
- Don’t repeat “multi-channel communications” language already covered in Core Competencies and Work Experience.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tool stack, but this item largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” It would be stronger if it emphasized methods/capabilities and trimmed generic terms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Analytics & Optimization Tools
- Tighten content to: GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing
- Replace “Dashboarding” with the actual tools already listed; “dashboarding” is a capability, not a platform.
- If accurate, swap “SEO” for a more specific tool or capability such as “Google Search Console” or “SEO analysis” to make the list more concrete.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” Consider keeping the broader capability framing there and using this section only for named tools.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already reinforced in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating generic analytics language elsewhere.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and foundational, with concrete outputs rather than team/operations language already covered in 2018–2024 entries.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-career build work: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and support multi-channel publishing across web, email, social and video.”
- Add clearer execution scope: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates for member and advocacy communications.”
- Tighten management phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “helped supervise a digital media associate.”
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, publishing cadence, audience reach, or website/email growth.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthening workflows” overlaps with later NACo bullets on governance/publishing systems.
- “Weekly video updates” is also mentioned in the 2018–2022 role; frame this item as launching or first producing the series.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around concrete ownership and outputs, while avoiding overlap with later digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize ownership and the standout achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and lead with action/result: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with a clearer scope, e.g. “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add volume or reach: number of episodes, stakeholders supported, or types of projects delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this entry focused on research/program support plus the podcast launch.
- Avoid claiming broader digital leadership here, since that is already covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a mixed list of software and capabilities. It also overlaps with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and several work bullets, so tighten it to emphasize tools only.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Multimedia & Creative Software
